changelog:
[pre-print cut 2026-08-02, rel#37] Reduce avg holdings 5.1→3.9 (max 9→6) via min_position_pct 1→12 — concentrate into higher-conviction momentum names for follow-ability. Improves CAGR 20.57→21.94, Martin 4.21→4.35, worst-12mo −6.3→−5.6, and 3 of 4 D6 metrics; sole D6 regression is longest-underwater +73d (deliberate).

[D6 regression accepted on longest underwater (d): Ticker reduction for manageability: concentrating into the top names lengthens the max underwater-vs-SPY stretch by ~73d, but improves CAGR +1.4pp, Martin, worst-12mo, and 3 of 4 D6 metrics (RDD3y, worst-3y-excess, cohorts). Deliberate net win on return, risk-efficiency, and follow-ability.]

[pre-print cut 2026-08-10, rel#38] Retire the ratchet re-risk override and arm cash momentum for an empty defensive sleeve. The allocator was computing posture from a fabricated defensive momentum of 0, which meant 'there are no bonds' rather than 'bonds returned zero'; it now uses the TBILL_13W trailing return over the same 18-month window, compared against UNDISCOUNTED risk momentum (the vol suppressor shrinks equity momentum multiplicatively, and zero was safe only as the fixed point of that shrink). Also relocates min_position_pct from book level to the equity sleeve so a position floor can no longer delete the entire bond book. CAGR 21.12% -> 20.93%; maxDD and worst-12mo bit-identical. D6: 3 of 4 instruments improve; cohorts-still-behind 1.10% -> 1.47% accepted, see the acceptance reason.

[D6 regression accepted on cohorts still behind: 3 of 4 D6 instruments IMPROVE, including longest-underwater 1284d -> 1199d and RDD3y 0.6428% -> 0.6157%. Only cohorts-still-behind regresses, 1.10% -> 1.47%, marginally past the 0.25pp materiality threshold (~18 more start-date cohorts out of ~5000). Taken because the change removes a posture computed from a fabricated input: with the bond sleeve empty the allocator read defensive momentum as 0, meaning 'there are no bonds' rather than 'bonds returned zero', and on 2022-11-01 that produced d=0.95 from a 1.16pp gap saturated by tau=0.004.]

[pre-print cut 2026-08-10, rel#39] Dust, caps, and an executor that was overruling the engine. (1) Bond sleeve arms k_per_allocation_pct: 10, which Preserve already had — Growth carried a sub-1% position in 29 of 248 reallocations against Preserve's 0. (2) min_position_breadth_pct: 6 replaces the crowd-month floor off-switch with a REDUCED floor. (3) min_sleeve_pct: 2 sweeps a de-minimis sleeve budget up, or down when nothing above can take it. (4) dust_prune_pct: 0.1 drops unexecutable slivers to CASH, never renormalizing across sleeves. (5) dynamic_k and the per-sleeve floor now respect the per-fund cap when redistributing after a drop; they were breaching the crowd-tightened cap in 4 of 248 months (ITA 53.02% against a 49.84% cap). (6) An empty target map means 100% CASH, not a failed rebalance — the executor was holding the previous book while the engine asked for cash. CAGR 20.93% -> 21.09%, Martin 4.087 -> 4.109, worst-12mo -5.14% -> -5.31%, maxDD unchanged; cap violations 4 -> 0; sub-2% dust months 34 -> 0. The 2022 bear now reads -4.31% rather than +0.78%: the engine wanted 100% cash on 2022-10-03 when every fund failed the gate, and the old executor rode the November bounce instead. Numbered v6.4 because v6.3 was cut, rolled back, and is permanently bound in the public version registry to a different fingerprint.

[pre-print cut 2026-08-16, rel#40] All-cash liquidation fix (empty target now trades to explicit CASH; Oct/Nov-2022 phantom hold removed) + revert of the v6.2 cash-momentum lever (ratchet back to 0, empty_defensive_momentum removed): the v6.2 adoption A/B was contaminated in every arm by the phantom hold; on the fixed engine honest V0 dominates on every axis. v6.3/v6.4 dust-and-cap work retained. True numbers: CAGR 20.72, worst-12mo -5.68, 2022 -1.1 vs SPY -18.2.

— superseded in place 2026-08-17 —
Retire downtrend_floor. It reads VOLATILITY despite its name (fast/slow SPY realized-vol ratio, never trend), its signal peaks at 1.61 against a ratio_hi of 1.8 so it never fully activates, and the pair ablation showed it INTERFERING with uptrend_ceiling. Removing it improves all four D6 instruments (RDD3y 0.578->0.478, worst-3y excess -14.41->-10.44, longest-underwater 907->906, cohorts 0.95->0.93), CAGR 20.72->20.90, Martin 3.902->3.941, and turnover 5.304->5.222, across 24 of 248 changed rebalances. Cost: worst-12mo -5.68->-6.83 (14% of its budget) and p90 position 43.70->44.56. That cost is STRUCTURAL, not a tuning gap — the vol_suppressor_k sweep (5..25) shows it worse at every k, and k=10 is an interior optimum on both configs; the degradation lands in the Q4-2018 vol spike, not in a crisis. Preserve never carried this lever, so Growth is now aligned with it.

— superseded in place 2026-08-20 —
Remove EquityCommodity.k_per_allocation_pct (was 25): retire a latent floor() discontinuity in the holding-count control. effectiveK = max(1, floor(sleevePct/kPer)), and 25 divides 100, so a fully-invested equity sleeve sat EXACTLY on floor(100/25)=4 in 188 of 234 reallocations (zero between 99.0 and 99.99%). Correct today, but any lever shaving 1pp off equity silently dropped the book to 3 names — which is what mis-credited uptrend_ceiling with +0.74pp of CAGR during the 2026-08-20 sensitivity sweep. Safe to remove because sleeve_min_position_pct 12 already enforces the same anti-fragmentation intent as a smooth WEIGHT floor: equity dynamic_k drops 93 -> 0, sleeve_min_position_floor 31 -> 65, months >40% concentration 50 -> 45, turnover 5.219 -> 5.116, cost drag -2.2k. Bond KEEPS its k_per_allocation_pct 10, where it does real work (363 of 456 drops). Cost: CAGR -0.12pp and Martin -0.017, both inside the 0.3pp/0.06 noise floor but both negative — buying structural robustness with an unmeasurable amount of return. Acceptance PASSED: worst-3y excess -10.44 -> -10.32, longest underwater 906 -> 903d, RDD3y immaterial. 43 of 248 rebalances change.

— superseded in place 2026-08-22 —
regimeAdaptiveMomentum days_below_threshold 110 -> 90. Dot-com regime insurance: buys +9.50pp of dot-com return and +5.56pp of dot-com maxDD (extended proxy basis, deltas only, n=1) for full-cycle costs INSIDE the noise floor (CAGR -0.18pp vs a 0.50pp bar; Martin -0.063 vs 0.100). Interior optimum (90 beats both 70 and 110 on dot-com maxDD; the axis worsens monotonically 90->130) and it replicates across regime references (VTI@90 -19.82%, SPY@90 -20.14%), so the effect is the threshold and not the benchmark. Executes the decision recorded at optimization-log.md:9040 which was never applied; it had lapsed because a later sensitivity run judged it on the live basis ONLY, where 90 loses. Under the dot-com-insurance arbiter it wins clearly. Full write-up: docs/engineering/research/regime-reference-2026-08.md

— superseded in place 2026-08-28 —
Three validated changes, additive to the decimal (+1.04pp CAGR, Martin 3.84 to 4.34, all four D6 instruments improved, every risk band at 0% spent; pnpm accept PASSED). (1) Extension penalty at selection: momentum-residualized extension demotes stretched leaders, offense-scoped, armed only while SPY is below its 200-day trend. (2) Clustering replaces the greedy pairwise dedup on the same correlation matrix at the same threshold; only the grouping changes. (3) The unjudged tier is handled on purpose: a fund the momentum-conditional screen cannot judge is scored on its idiosyncratic tail (unconditional forward return with the market crash months removed), with the high-volatility band exempt so cyclicals are judged on correlation, not crash risk. Menu byte-identical to the prior champion in every year. Research: docs/engineering/research/menu-screen-2026-08.md and extension-penalty.md.
